    13	/-!
    14	# The ε frame cover, keyed on the WINDOW QUOTIENT rather than on a carrier
    15	
    16	Roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.framecover-aff`.
    17	
    18	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffFraming.lean` established that the ε-pair and its pair-chart framing
    19	clause are expressible over the widened carrier, and recorded what it did not do:
    20	
    21	> It does not prove `exists_certChartCover` over the widened carrier — that theorem's proof
    22	> runs the certificate cover and the per-piece frame covers, which is real work and belongs to
    23	> whoever restates it.
    24	
    25	**This file measures that work, and the measurement is the content.**  Inside
    26	`exists_frame_chart_at_prime` the frame-cover keystone `divFamEps_exists_frameCover`
    27	(`Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean:456`) reads its carrier `DivFam C S π g` at **eight** sites, of
    28	**two** kinds:
    29	
    30	* **six** are facts about the window *quotient* — `DivFam.finite_/projective_window_quotient`
    31	  at each of the two ledger windows (:347–357), and `F.window` in the `exists_away_free_pair`
    32	  call (:361, :365).  Constant fibre rank enters separately, through `divFamWindowGr`'s own
    33	  definition.  These are what the layer below restates as hypotheses.
    34	* **two** are *functoriality* of the carrier: `DivFam.window_mapAlg` in the closing `rfl` blocks
    35	  (:426, :443), i.e. "window of `mapAlg` = `windowBaseChange`".  These are **not** window-quotient
    36	  facts, and they are exactly what `windowBaseChange_windowBaseChange` below had to replace.
    37	
    38	Everything downstream of the helper — `exists_component_matrix`,
    39	`exists_det_submatrix_notMem_of_mul_eq_one`, `exists_away_isUnit_of_notMem`,
    40	`map_component_chart` — consumes a Grassmannian *point* and a base ring, and never asks what
    41	produced the submodule.
    42	
    43	*A predecessor version of this paragraph said "exactly three points" and listed
    44	finite/projective/rankAtStalk.  That both under-counted the reads and mis-classified the two
    45	that motivated this file's one new theorem; corrected here (audit `I-1336`).*
    46	
    47	`divisorWindow d hH1` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean:103`) is independent of the
    48	**adaptation** — of which cover refines `d` — which is what lets the declarations below typecheck
    49	carrier-free.  It is **not** independent of the pinned charts: it is a `Submodule.comap` of
    50	`d.vanishingSubmodule R (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ … .V₁ …`, so the fixed two-chart pair
    51	occurs in its definition.  *A predecessor version said "no adaptation, no cover and no chart
    52	typing"; only the first clause is true (`I-1336`).*
    53	
    54	## The one step that is genuinely new
    55	
    56	Restating the layer with the three facts as hypotheses is free, but the tower transport is
    57	not.  The chart-typed `map_divFamWindowGr` (`Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean:188`) proves
    58	`Grassmannian.map β (point over R_h) = point over R_u` by routing through the divisor
    59	*object* — `DivFam.window_mapAlg` on both legs plus `DivFam.mapAlg_comp` — which needs a
    60	carrier with a functorial `mapAlg`.  Carrier-free there is no object to route through, so the
    61	composite must be proved where it actually lives, on the submodule:
    62	
    63	* `windowBaseChange_windowBaseChange` — transitivity of the window pushforward over a tower
    64	  `R → R' → R''`, for an arbitrary `k`-module ambient `H`.  Not in the tree before; both
    65	  inclusions are `windowBaseChange_le_iff` against the compared generators, and the content
    66	  is one `cancelBaseChange` compatibility (`rfl` fails on it, checked).
    67	
    68	## What this does and does NOT establish
    69	
    70	It does **not** produce a widened divisor-representability, and no antecedent of
    71	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` moves.  The window-quotient facts are **hypotheses** in the window
    72	layer.  The `Reachability` section below gives the chart-typed route to them; the correct ledger
    73	for the *widened* route is:
    74	
    75	  the frame cover's chart dependence   REMOVED (this file, sorry-free)
    76	  its window-quotient inputs           reachable chart-typed (below), and reachable WIDENED by
    77	                                       the same three-line proofs through
    78	                                       `AffAdaptation.windowQuotEquiv`
    79	                                       (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean:914`) — whose source
    80	                                       is the SAME quotient — gated on surjectivity of the
    81	                                       widened `thetaGluedEval`, which that file leaves OPEN.
    82	
    83	**Two corrections to predecessor versions of this docstring, both from an audit
    84	(`I-1335`/`I-1337`) that I reproduced before accepting.**  I first wrote that the inputs "reduce
    85	to widened evaluation surjectivity"; I then over-corrected to "the ONE route that exists" plus
    86	"REFUTED on the straddling divisors".  The second is worse than the first and is the one to
    87	retract loudly:
    88	
    89	* the widened route **exists** and is gated on a *missing proof*, not on a refutation;
    90	* and the straddling no-go **cannot** bear on it, because
    91	  `forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` quantifies over `DivisorAdaptation` while the widened
    92	  route consumes `AffAdaptation`.  On exactly those divisors,
    93	  `isCertified_affine_and_not_isCertified_chart` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean`) proves
    94	  the *opposite* conjunction: some widened adaptation IS certified while no chart-typed one is.
    95	  So there the widened side is the one that works, and the no-go is evidence *for* it.
    96	
    97	One nuance neither the audit nor I had stated, added here because it is the actual widened
    98	residue: `AffAdaptation.windowQuotEquiv` also takes a `ChartTyping C R π D`, and
    99	`AffAdaptation.isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling` (same file) *empties* that index on a piece
   100	holding a point outside `V₀` and one outside `V₁`.  So the widened route owes **both** the
   101	evaluation surjectivity and a chart typing (or a `ThetaTrivData`-style replacement index — see
   102	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean`, inhabited at exponent `0`).  That is a second missing
   103	input, still not a refutation.
   104	
   105	## Main declarations
   106	
   107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divisorWindowGrOfQuot` — the window as a Grassmannian point from the
   108	  quotient certificate alone; `divFamWindowGr` with its vehicle removed.
   109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.windowBaseChange_windowBaseChange` — transitivity of the window
   110	  pushforward.
   111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.map_divisorWindowGrOfQuot` — the tower transport, carrier-free.
   112	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_component_matrix_of_windowQuot` — the per-prime matrix
   113	  presentation, carrier-free.
   114	* `AlgebraicGeometry.finite_divisorWindow_quot_of_isCertified` and its two siblings — the
   115	  chart-typed supply of the hypotheses.
   116	-/

   167	/-- **The window as a Grassmannian point, from the quotient certificate alone**: the

   202	This is the step the chart-typed transport did NOT have to prove: `map_divFamWindowGr`
   203	(`Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean:188`) reaches the same conclusion by going *through the
   204	divisor object* — `DivFam.window_mapAlg` on both legs plus `DivFam.mapAlg_comp` — which needs
   205	a carrier with a functorial `mapAlg`.  Carrier-free there is no object to route through, so

   210	theorem windowBaseChange_windowBaseChange {H : Type u} [AddCommGroup H] [Module k H]
   211	    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   212	    (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']
   213	    (R'' : Type u) [CommRing R''] [Algebra k R''] [Algebra R R''] [Algebra R' R'']
   214	    [IsScalarTower k R R''] [IsScalarTower k R' R''] [IsScalarTower R R' R'']
   215	    (N : Submodule R (R ⊗[k] H)) :
   216	    windowBaseChange R'' (windowBaseChange R' N) = windowBaseChange R'' N := by
   217	  -- the `R'`-linear comparison arrow `R' ⊗[k] H → R'' ⊗[k] H` of the upper leg
   218	  set ψ : (R' ⊗[k] H) →ₗ[R'] (R'' ⊗[k] H) :=
   219	    (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange k R' R'' R'' H).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
   220	      (TensorProduct.mk R' R'' (R' ⊗[k] H) 1) with hψdef
   221	  have hψ : ∀ y : R' ⊗[k] H, ψ y
   222	      = TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange k R' R'' R'' H (1 ⊗ₜ y) :=
   223	    fun _ => rfl
   224	  -- the tower compatibility of the comparison: the two legs agree on the lower generators
   225	  have key : ∀ x : R ⊗[k] H,
   226	      ψ (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange k R R' R' H (1 ⊗ₜ x))
   227	        = TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange k R R'' R'' H (1 ⊗ₜ x) := by
   228	    intro x
   229	    induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   230	    | zero => simp
   231	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add, hx, hy]
   232	    | tmul r h => simp [hψ]
   233	  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
   234	  · -- `⊆`: test the upper generators, then the lower ones through `ψ`
   235	    rw [windowBaseChange_le_iff]
   236	    have hstep : windowBaseChange R' N
   237	        ≤ Submodule.comap ψ ((windowBaseChange R'' N).restrictScalars R') := by
   238	      rw [windowBaseChange_le_iff]
   239	      intro x hx
   240	      refine Submodule.mem_comap.mpr ?_
   241	      rw [key x]
   242	      exact cancelBaseChange_one_tmul_mem_windowBaseChange hx
   243	    intro y hy
   244	    rw [← hψ y]
   245	    exact hstep hy
   246	  · -- `⊇`: a lower generator is `ψ` of an upper generator
   247	    rw [windowBaseChange_le_iff]
   248	    intro x hx
   249	    rw [← key x, hψ]
   250	    exact cancelBaseChange_one_tmul_mem_windowBaseChange
   251	      (cancelBaseChange_one_tmul_mem_windowBaseChange hx)

it needs reduces to ONE hypothesis: IsPlusHonest (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200). Read as a
statement, that says: for every affine open U of the test, the class restricted to U lies in the
RANGE of relPicToPicEt -- i.e. Zariski-locally the class comes from the UN-sheafified relPic.

That is the etale-sheafification gap, structurally:
 * picEt is built on PicEtAff (PicEt.lean:9-21), and PicEtAff C A (PicEtAff.lean:218) is a QUOTIENT
   OVER ALL ETALE COVERS -- elements are PicEtAff.mk E x;
 * PicEtAff.unit (:377), the target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126), is mk at the TRIVIAL
   cover `.self A` alone.

one-step plus construction exists to permit to FAIL. The tree's only honesty mechanism agrees:
Pic0ChartHonest.lean's own "does not give" says honesty holds over Spec E.Carrier and NOT over
Spec A, bought by CHANGING THE BASE, with "Nothing here performs that descent".

pessimism: chartValue = abelDiv * sigmaFamily * (thetaFamily^m)^{-1} (DivSchemeAbel.lean:351, read
from the definition), and honesty is discharged for each factor and closed under the group
operations. Coverage is different because chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise
(Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) quantifies over EVERY s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T);
arbitrariness is the content of coverage, and narrowing s to chart-value shape makes it circular.

them: honesty of coverage's own WITNESS is already covered; honesty of the class coverage must HIT
is the gap. The repair -- refine to the etale carrier, then descend -- changes the site from Zariski
to etale, and pic0RepresentableByOfCharts' antecedent is Zariski-local surjectivity. No leaf settles
that. It is a route question for the human/reviewer layer, and it is the third antecedent-level
obstruction found on this seam after the unrestricted-certificate fork (antecedent 1) and U2.

Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. ["I-1530","open",null,"A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.

WHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.

WHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.

THE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.

THE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted."]

["I-1629","open",null,"A "TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.

WHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: "going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.

It is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.

THE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing "route X does not work", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.

COROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check."]

["I-1630","open",null,"[persistent] The "25 open tasks (max 12)" warning is 8 round lanes + 17 durable charters, and no lane can act on it as phrased

MEASURED (janitor pass, pic-e 0095 r5). Of 25 open tasks: 3 `running` (pic-c, pic-e, pic-g) each matching a live pid in `horizon ps` (0092, 0095, 0096) — no orphaned `running` status; 5 more `pic-*` lanes `queued` between rounds of the same eight-lane round I-1482 describes; and 17 non-lane `queued` tasks that are project CHARTERS and wave objectives (`T16`, `rebuild`, `ajc-*`, `ajcr-*`), not backlog.

WHY THIS NEEDS A DECISION, NOT A CLEANUP. Cancelling a charter deletes a project target statement; leaving them re-fires the warning on every command for every lane. The eight lane tasks are also structurally permanent for the round — a lane between rounds is `queued`, so the count cannot drop below 8 while the fleet is 8 wide.

An earlier janitor established the same conclusion for a 13-task queue (archived I-0648, "8 running + 5 charters"); it was archived and the derivation is being repeated each pass. Filing it open and `[persistent]` so it stops being re-derived. Same shape as I-1607 for the roadmap active-count warning: cap-vs-semantics, and the fix is a config/semantics choice, not an item edit."]

["I-1607","open",null,"The roadmap's "24 active items (max 8)" warning is 14 CONE rows, not 14 competing fronts -- decide whether cones should be active at all, because nobody can act on the warning as phrased.

MEASURED (janitor pass, run 0096). Of the 24 `active` rows, 14 have children and 10 are leaves. Every cone is unowned and is active because its subtree is in progress: AJC.jacobian (8 children), AJC.picrep (19), AJCR.w4-rep.datum (21), AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate (21), and ten more. The genuine parallel fronts are the 10 leaves, and 8 of those carry a live lane owner (pic-b, pic-c, pic-d, pic-e, pic-f x2, pic-h) with only `AJC.picrep.etale-rep.quotient-hom` and `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.chart-restrict` active-and-unowned.

WHY THIS NEEDS A DECISION RATHER THAN A CLEANUP. Setting a cone to `pending` while its children are being worked is a lie about the board; leaving it `active` re-fires the warning every command for every lane. Neither is a janitor call. Two candidate resolutions: (a) treat `active` on a parent as meaning "this subtree is the focus" and raise/ignore the advisory cap, or (b) reserve `active` for leaves and let cone status be derived from the `n/m done` progress the renderer already shows. I did not change any status.

The 8 lane-owned leaves are consistent with the eight-lane round protection I-1482 describes, so the leaf count is not the problem."]

["I-0144","open",null,"Duplicate Spec-of-algebra-map Over-morphisms: `AlgebraicGeometry.overSpecMap` vs `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.overSpecMap`

While blueprinting the Wave-4 CBC bricks I found two near-identical Lean declarations for "Spec of an algebra map as a morphism in Over (Spec k)":

- `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.overSpecMap (f : A →ₐ[k] B) : overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A` — `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RelPicAlgebra.lean:44`, widely used in the Picard lane (blueprinted at `def:overSpecMap` in `PicardEtale.tex`).
- `AlgebraicGeometry.overSpecMap : overSpec k R' ⟶ overSpec k R` — `AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:147`, taking the map through `[Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']` instead of an explicit `AlgHom` (now blueprinted, bound together with `relCurveMap` at `def:relCurveMap` in `Cohomology.tex`).

Same mathematics, different packaging; the root-namespace name shadows the `Over` one under `open`. **Suggested cleanup for a Horizon agent:** define the CBC one as `Over.overSpecMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k R R')` (or inline it), then rebind the blueprint node. Not urgent; both are kernel-green. No blueprint action needed — the two nodes are honest about which declaration each binds."]

["I-1706","open",null,"Reduction between two already-complete characterizations adds framing, not reach

pic-c's `mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_of_map_reduced` (coboundary over A iff over A/nil) is genuine, non-vacuous, axiom-clean; its converse `laurentCoboundaryUnits_map` really is free and distinct, so NOT a re-spelling of its hypothesis.

- But the arbitrary-ring question it "reduces" was ALREADY fully settled by `mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff_general` (coboundary iff C c·(1+z), c unit, z nilpotent); reduced case by `iff_reduced`.
- `not_tUnit_general` is directly re-derivable from `iff_general` at any nontrivial ring, without the reduced-quotient detour.
- Lesson: when auditing a "THE REDUCTION" keystone, check whether BOTH endpoints are already characterized upstream; if so the value is structural/expository for a consumer, not new reachability. Correctness/cleanliness here: fine."]

["I-1504","open",null,"STALE index.lock ON THE SHARED LEDGER BLOCKS EVERY LANE'S SHARED-INDEX WRITE -- and it is currently the only thing preventing a staged-D clobber. Do not delete it without reading the second half of this item.

MEASURED (pic-g, run 0096). .archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git/index.lock is ZERO BYTES, mtime 2026-07-30 11:54:57, ~80 minutes old at time of writing. No holder: lsof on the lock returns nothing, and `ps -eo cmd | grep 'git --git-dir'` finds no live git against this git-dir. Every `git add` to the SHARED index (GIT_INDEX_FILE unset) fails with 'Unable to create ... index.lock: File exists'. I retried 45 times over 2 minutes.

WHAT IT BLOCKS. The I-1222 remediation step. That protection tells a lane whose path is staged D in the shared index to clear it with an explicit `add`. That is now impossible. My own Pic0ChartMultiIndexInterval.lean is staged D right now and I cannot clear it.

WHY I DID NOT REMOVE THE LOCK, and this is the part worth thinking about before someone does. The shared index currently holds 152 staged deletions, 11 of them .lean across BOTH projects (AJCR: DivisorFamilyAffFibreData, DivisorFamilyDegreeZero, DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique, Pic0ChartMultiIndexInterval; AJC: DivFamilyZero, FiniteMorphismEmbedding, GaloisDescent/PicEtGaloisCover, H0SemicontinuityInstance, ProjectiveMorphismBasic, ProjectiveSpaceAffineChart, ProjectiveSpaceAffineChartRing). I verified mine is present BOTH at HEAD and on disk. The hazard I-1222 describes is a lane committing that whole index as a tree. The lock makes that commit impossible too. So while the lock is held, the staged deletions are INERT -- removing the lock re-arms them.

THE ORDER TO DO IT IN, if a lane or human clears the lock: (1) confirm no live git holder, as above; (2) remove the lock; (3) IMMEDIATELY re-add all 11 .lean paths to the shared index, not just your own -- the census above is the enumeration, and per memory 'enumerate-the-index-not-your-files' a census seeded from your own work is blind exactly where the blast radius is someone else's; (4) verify each is present at HEAD and on disk before assuming an add is the right repair rather than a restore. Doing (2) without (3) is strictly worse than leaving the lock.

Fresh-index committing (rm -f a private index file, read-tree HEAD, add explicit paths, commit with GIT_INDEX_FILE set) is UNAFFECTED -- it does not touch the shared index or its lock. I landed 6 commits that way this session with clean post-commit HEAD~1..HEAD stats. So this blocks remediation, not work."]

Statement-preserving; no proof changes; root gains two import lines.

OWNER: any janitor/hygiene pass or the next lane that edits the file. Do NOT split while sibling lanes are consuming it mid-flight without checking horizon ps / live-lane state first."]

Usage: horizon inbox add [OPTIONS]                                             
                                                                                
 Add a local inbox item.                                                        
                                                                                
 ``--persistent``/``--temporary`` are sugar: they prepend a ```` or             
 ```` tag to the body, which is the only signal agents read to decide           
 whether to keep or close the item. ``--to`` addresses the item to a recipient  
 (e.g. ``--to project:foo`` to message another project).
